subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Influencer Effect
description: A micro-lesson that makes Influencer Effect usable.

hook.text: A fitness influencer holds a protein bar. She does not say it is good. She just holds it. Sales jump 40% that week.

buildup.text: Influencer marketing works through parasocial relationships. Followers feel they know and trust the influencer.

discovery.text: The persuasion is implicit. Association with a trusted person transfers trust to the product without explicit argument.

twist.text: Micro-influencers with 10K followers often drive higher engagement than celebrities.

climax.text: When an influencer features a product, ask: is this genuine use or paid placement?

punchline.text: You trust the person. They are selling the product.

quiz.question: Why are micro-influencers often more effective than celebrities?
options: Their smaller audiences feel more personal and trustworthy
They always use the products they promote
